subproblem.title: Shifted-ball comparison: two ball integrals differ by at most K times the measure of an annulus
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, x, w ∈ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), and ρ, K ∈ ℝ with ‖w‖ ≤ ρ and K ≥ 0. Let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable on B̆_{ρ+‖w‖}(x) with |u(z)| ≤ K for all z ∈ B̆_{ρ+‖w‖}(x). Let ω := Lⁿ(B̆_1(0)) as a real number. Then |∫_{B̆_ρ(x+w)} u − ∫_{B̆_ρ(x)} u| ≤ K·ω·((ρ + ‖w‖)ⁿ − (ρ − ‖w‖)ⁿ). In Lean the first integral must be parenthesized; otherwise the set-integral notation absorbs `- ∫ …` into its integrand.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (x w : Euclid n) (ρ K : ℝ), 0 < n → ‖w‖ ≤ ρ → 0 ≤ K → IntegrableOn u (ball x (ρ + ‖w‖)) → (∀ z ∈ ball x (ρ + ‖w‖), |u z| ≤ K) → |(∫ y in ball (x + w) ρ, u y) - ∫ y in ball x ρ, u y| ≤ K * (volume (ball (0 : Euclid n) 1)).toReal * ((ρ + ‖w‖) ^ n - (ρ - ‖w‖) ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected parent proof, first three bullets: the comparison of the integrals of u over B̆_ρ(x+ta) and B̆_ρ(x) through their symmetric difference and the annulus A_t. Here the shift ta is a general vector w and |t| is s := ‖w‖.

Notation.
- s := ‖w‖, so 0 ≤ s ≤ ρ; ω := (Lⁿ(B̆_1(0))).toReal.
- B₁ := ball(x + w, ρ), B₀ := ball(x, ρ), S₁ := B₁ \ B₀, S₂ := B₀ \ B₁.
- A := ball(x, ρ+s) \ ball(x, ρ−s).
All these sets are Borel, since balls are open.

1. Containment. For z ∈ B₁, ‖z − x‖ ≤ ‖z − (x + w)‖ + ‖w‖ < ρ + s. Also B₀ ⊆ ball(x, ρ+s) because s ≥ 0. So B₁, B₀, S₁, S₂ all lie in ball(x, ρ+s), which has finite measure. Consequently u is integrable on B₁ and on B₀ (IntegrableOn.mono_set), and |u| ≤ K on S₁ and S₂.

2. Splitting. Split each ball along the other (integral_inter_add_diff):
∫_{B₁} u = ∫_{B₁∩B₀} u + ∫_{S₁} u and ∫_{B₀} u = ∫_{B₀∩B₁} u + ∫_{S₂} u.
Since B₁ ∩ B₀ = B₀ ∩ B₁, subtracting gives ∫_{B₁} u − ∫_{B₀} u = ∫_{S₁} u − ∫_{S₂} u.

3. Bounding each piece. Each S_j has finite measure and |u| ≤ K on S_j, so |∫_{S_j} u| ≤ K·(Lⁿ(S_j)).toReal (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const). Hence |∫_{B₁} u − ∫_{B₀} u| ≤ K·((Lⁿ(S₁)).toReal + (Lⁿ(S₂)).toReal).

4. Disjointness. S₁ ⊆ B₁ and S₂ ∩ B₁ = ∅, so S₁ ∩ S₂ = ∅. Therefore Lⁿ(S₁) + Lⁿ(S₂) = Lⁿ(S₁ ∪ S₂) (measure_union), and the same holds for the real values since all are finite.

5. The symmetric difference lies in the annulus: S₁ ∪ S₂ ⊆ A.
- For z ∈ S₁: z ∉ B₀ gives ‖z − x‖ ≥ ρ ≥ ρ − s, and step 1 gives ‖z − x‖ < ρ + s.
- For z ∈ S₂: z ∈ B₀ gives ‖z − x‖ < ρ ≤ ρ + s, and z ∉ B₁ gives ‖z − x‖ ≥ ‖z − (x + w)‖ − ‖w‖ ≥ ρ − s.
In both cases z ∈ ball(x, ρ+s) and z ∉ ball(x, ρ−s). Hence Lⁿ(S₁ ∪ S₂) ≤ Lⁿ(A) (measure_mono).

6. Measure of the annulus. Since n ≥ 1, ℝⁿ is nontrivial, and for r ≥ 0, Lⁿ(ball(z, r)) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)·Lⁿ(B̆_1(0)) (Measure.addHaar_ball with finrank ℝ (Euclid n) = n, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin); its real value is ω·rⁿ. Since 0 ≤ ρ − s ≤ ρ + s, ball(x, ρ−s) ⊆ ball(x, ρ+s), and both have finite measure. So Lⁿ(A) = Lⁿ(ball(x, ρ+s)) − Lⁿ(ball(x, ρ−s)) (measure_diff), i.e. (Lⁿ(A)).toReal = ω(ρ+s)ⁿ − ω(ρ−s)ⁿ.

7. Conclusion. Since K ≥ 0, steps 2–6 give |∫_{B₁} u − ∫_{B₀} u| ≤ K·Lⁿ(S₁ ∪ S₂) ≤ K·Lⁿ(A) = K·ω·((ρ+s)ⁿ − (ρ−s)ⁿ), with s = ‖w‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: Both balls B̆_ρ(x+w) and B̆_ρ(x) lie in B̆_{ρ+‖w‖}(x), so u is integrable on them and bounded by K there.
|∫_{S_j} u| ≤ K·Lⁿ(S_j); S₁ and S₂ are disjoint, and their union lies in the annulus B̆_{ρ+‖w‖}(x) ∖ B̆_{ρ−‖w‖}(x) by the triangle inequality.
Lⁿ(annulus) = ω((ρ+‖w‖)ⁿ − (ρ−‖w‖)ⁿ) by Measure.addHaar_ball and measure_diff.

audit.reason: The parenthesized integral difference has the intended Lean parsing. The hypotheses imply nonnegative radii, including the zero-radius case. Integrability, measurable disjoint differences, annulus containment and finite-measure subtraction are all justified. The n > 0 hypothesis supplies the nontrivial-space condition for Haar scaling at radius zero.
